analyst_view.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9, so both still have plenty at stake: Okan Buruk's side want to push into the top 24 at home, Villa want a top-8 place. Galatasaray have a long injury list that the numbers do not carry (their missing list is empty): Victor Osimhen had knee surgery on 7 November and has not trained on the pitch yet, so at best he makes the bench, Rafael Leão is on a treatment programme aimed at a return on 8 December, and Roland Sallai and Ismail Jakobs (groin strain found on 20 November) are reported out. Villa have their own doubts: Matty Cash is in concussion protocol, Johan Manzambi is uncertain after leaving Switzerland's squad, and Ruggeri, Wan-Bissaka and Onana are out or not ready. Galatasaray's league game this weekend was moved away from RAMS Park for pitch work, but this match is back there; no referee is named yet. I trim Galatasaray's attacking numbers a little and leave the rest with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals (1.3 Galatasaray, 1.7 Villa) and list no absences. I lean lower: Osimhen (knee surgery, at most a bench role), Leão and Sallai are all missing for Galatasaray, which takes a big part of their front line away, though they did score freely in recent league games without Osimhen (17 in their last 6, already counted) and Villa's defence is thin with Cash and Wan-Bissaka doubtful, so the cut stays small: about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's recent rise in corners won (+3%) and Villa's dip (-3.7%). Losing Leão and Sallai on the wings could cost Galatasaray a little width, while Jakobs' absence at left-back cuts both ways, so I see no clear reason to move and stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, split evenly, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-2.7%) already taken off. RAMS Park is a loud, hostile place for visitors, but that is part of Galatasaray's home record the numbers use, and no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots (13.1 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa). Without Osimhen, Leão and Sallai, Galatasaray lose most of their usual shot-takers, which the numbers do not know about, so I trim the total by about 5% to roughly 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+3.3%). Galatasaray's missing forwards matter most for shot quality, Osimhen above all, so I lean a little lower, to about 9.6.
